log.content:
In graph theory terms, this problem asks for the maximum number of pairs of non-adjacent vertices (non-friends) that share a common neighbor (common friend) in a graph of $N=456$ vertices.

Let $G$ be the graph representing friendships. We are seeking to maximize the number of edges in $G^2$ that are not in $G$, excluding the diagonal. It is a known result in extremal graph theory that this quantity is maximized when the graph is a star graph, $K_{1, N-1}$.

In the star graph $K_{1, 455}$, there is one central participant $C$ and $N-1=455$ peripheral participants $L_1, L_2, \ldots, L_{455}$. The only friendships are between $C$ and every $L_i$.

The pairs that are not friends must be two peripheral participants, say $\{L_i, L_j\}$ ($i \neq j$). Any such pair $\{L_i, L_j\}$ is not friends, but they both share the common friend $C$.
The total number of such pairs is the number of ways to choose 2 participants from the $N-1$ peripheral participants:
$$\binom{N-1}{2} = \binom{455}{2}$$

Calculating this value:
$$\binom{455}{2} = \frac{455 \times (455 - 1)}{2} = \frac{455 \times 454}{2} = 455 \times 227 = 103285$$

The maximum possible number of such pairs is 103,285.
